analysis:
The supplied units contain only a CHANGELOG.md change. CHANGELOG.md:3-5 (head) adds an entry stating that `darkbloom update` and `darkbloom restart` now wait up to 60 s for launchd to release the drained job before bootstrapping it again. Per that entry, a failed relaunch re-arms the watchdog when auto-restart is on. No source code for the launchd or watchdog changes was supplied. This is a coverage limit, not evidence of safety.

The next pass should examine the actual provider lifecycle source for the following:
- T-043 (TB-003): whether watchdog rollback authority remains the same replaceable binary.
- Whether re-arming the watchdog on failure could loop or trigger unintended rollback.
- Whether the 60 s wait could strand a provider: an availability-only concern; laptop-shutdown-style DoS is out of scope.
- Whether the relaunch path preserves the drain semantics referenced in the v0.9.8 notes.
- T-010 cancellation propagation.
- That the relaunch does not bypass App Attest or legacy re-attestation (TB-011/T-053, connection-bound authorization on new process endpoints).

The base changelog text is historical and introduces no new code behavior. No security finding is supported by documentation alone.
